 Oral Judgment

(PER: THE HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR) MFA No.21893/2012 is filed by the Insurance Company seeking reduction of compensation awarded on the ground that the same is exorbitant, whereas MFA CROB No.100162/2015 is filed by the claimants/cross objectors seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. Both these appeals are filed being aggrieved by the common judgment and award dated 23.02.2012 passed in MVC No.1924/2011 by the Fast Tract Court-II and Additional MACT, Belgaum (for short, 'Tribunal').

entities.text: Fast Tract Court-II and Additional MACT, Belgaum
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Brief facts giving rise to filing of these appeals are that on 12.02.2011, the deceased Sonu S/o Ramkeval Prajapati (for short, 'deceased') was going from Shahunagar to Nanwadi by riding his bicycle and also his friend Indresh Prajapati was going along with him on separate bicycle and when they were going near the spot i.e., AMPC road, opposite to laxmi complex Sadashiv Nagar, Belgaum,
at that time, a tipper bearing registration NC: 2025:KHC-D:7346 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100162 of 2015 HC-KAR No.KA-25/A-7931 came from behind and dashed to deceased bicycle from hind side.
As a result of which, the deceased fell down and the said tipper ran over the body of deceased.

Later,
the deceased was succumbed to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
Thus, the claimants being legal heirs of the deceased have filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act'), seeking compensation.

4. Heard arguments and perused the material placed on record.
5.

In this case, the Tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads.

Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Towards medical expenses.

34,621/-
 2. Towards loss of dependency.

4,72,500/-
 3. Towards funeral expenses.

15,000/-
 4. Towards love and affection in 15,000/-
 respect of petitioner 1 and 2.

5. Towards transportation of dead 2,000/-
 body.

Total: 5,39,121/-
 NC: 2025:KHC-D:7346 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100162 of 2015 HC-KAR 6.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.5,39,121/- along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petitions till its realization.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co., Ltd vs Ramkeval S/O Badariprasad Prajapate
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insofar as quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has not taken correct parameters.
The accident occurred on 12.02.2011.
The deceased was aged 20 years old at the time of accident and was working as a carpenter under the main contractor Shir.
Hence, the notional income is to be taken at Rs.6,000/- per month, as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, considering the age of the deceased, 40% of the income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased was a bachelor.
Therefore, 50% of the income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

Considering the age of the deceased, the appropriate applicable multiplier is '18'.
NC: 2025:KHC-D:7346 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100162 of 2015 HC-KAR
Therefore, loss of dependency is re-
assessed and quantified at Rs.9,07,200/- (Rs.6,000 + 40% minus 50% x 12 x 18).

8. In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LIMITED V. NANU RAM & OTHERS, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782 and in the case of PRANAY SETHI (SUPRA), the claimants are entitled for Rs.40,000/- under the head 'loss of consortium', along with 10% escalation.

entities.text: MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LIMITED V. NANU RAM & OTHERS, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are two dependents i.e., his father and mother.
Accordingly, Rs.88,000/- (Rs.40,000 x 2 + 10%) is awarded under the head 'loss of consortium including loss of love and affection'.

Further, the claimants are entitled to Rs.16,500/- (15,000 x 2 +
10%) each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses including 10% escalation.

9. Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation under various heads as under:
NC: 2025:KHC-D:7346 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100162 of 2015 HC-KAR Particulars

Amount (in Rs.) Towards loss of dependency 9,07,200/- Towards loss of estate and 33,000/- transportation of dead body and funeral expenses Towards loss of consortium 88,000/-
 Total 10,28,200/-
 10.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.10,28,200/- as against Rs.5,39,121/- awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
The Tribunal has awarded interest on the compensation at 9% per annum, which is scaled down to 6% per annum, since this Court is consistently awarding interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

11. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i. Appeal as well as cross objection are allowed in part.
